summary:
MoonWindow is an intuitive, aerospace-grade web application engineered for rapid, date-resilient landing site evaluation across the Lunar South Pole (80°S–90°S). Future Artemis and commercial CLPS missions face extreme polar constraints: the Sun skims the horizon at 1.5°, casting 40-kilometer shadows, while Earth wobbles on the skyline, threatening direct-to-Earth (DTE) communications. In reality, launch dates slip due to hardware or weather holds; a 72-hour delay can rotate the landing phase and plunge a planned sunlit site into a fatal 80-hour cryogenic blackout.

MoonWindow bridges high-precision NASA LOLA altimetry and SPICE orbital ephemeris with an agile dual-axis screening model: planners can evaluate "Change only the date" (launch window slips from +0 to +14 days) or "Change only the site" (Connecting Ridge, Malapert Massif, Peak of Light, Nobile VIPER). The platform renders an interactive 3D WebGL lunar globe, casts real-time 360° local crater rim obstacle skylines to assess power and communication clearance, and computes hazard-constrained Dijkstra rover traverses to cryogenic water-ice Permanently Shadowed Regions (PSRs). By turning hours of offline GIS scripting into millisecond visual trade studies, MoonWindow empowers flight planners, educators, and the public.
details:
1. WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS

MoonWindow transforms complex lunar topography and celestial mechanics into instantaneous flight-readiness verdicts across the Lunar South Pole (80°S–90°S). It operates via a dual-axis evaluation framework:

• "Change Only the Date": Planners hold a candidate landing site constant while scrubbing the 29.5-day synodic lunar cycle or simulating Launch Window Slips (+0 to +14 days) to verify whether solar array generation and battery storage survive unexpected delays.

• "Change Only the Site": Planners hold the launch date constant and compare candidate landing zones (Connecting Ridge, Malapert Massif, Peak of Light, Nobile VIPER, or custom coordinates) side-by-side.

• 360° Local Horizon Radar: MoonWindow casts rays in 72 azimuth bins (5° resolution) over NASA LOLA elevation data, calculating the obstacle elevation angle h(θ) = max [arctan((H_k - H_0)/d_k)] to plot exact clearance margins for Sun and Earth above surrounding crater rims.

• Surface Mobility Engine: An 8-neighbor Dijkstra least-cost routing engine computes traversable rover trajectories from touchdown points to volatile cold traps in Permanently Shadowed Regions (PSRs), enforcing chassis slope limits (≤ 15°) and solar illumination preferences while plotting an interactive elevation profile.

2. BENEFITS & INTENDED IMPACT

• Flight Planning Agility: Reduces landing site trade studies from hours of offline GIS scripts and SPICE kernel wrangling to under 100 milliseconds of interactive visual screening.

• Mission Risk Mitigation: Prevents catastrophic battery discharge and communication loss caused by unforeseen crater rim occultation following launch scrubs.

• Universal Accessibility: Provides two-tier UX: plain-language operational summaries ("Nominal landing zone. High solar power, direct Earth line-of-sight, gentle slope") for students and educators, alongside granular mathematical telemetry for aerospace engineers.

3. TOOLS, LANGUAGES & SOFTWARE USED

• Frontend & Rendering: HTML5 Canvas, WebGL, Three.js r128 with custom polar planar orthographic geometry, OrbitControls, and ACES Filmic tone mapping.

• Programming: Modern ECMAScript (ES6+), Web Audio API, and CSS3 responsive layout with zero build friction.

• Ephemeris Physics: Analytical models for lunar obliquity (1.5427°), draconic month (27.212d), synodic month (29.531d), and optical libration in latitude (±6.68°) and longitude (±7.91°).

• Data Sources: NASA LRO LOLA Digital Elevation Models (267 m/cell resolution), NASA SPICE ephemeris, and Artemis III candidate site catalogs.

• Deployment: GitHub Pages continuous deployment via automated GitHub Actions workflows.

4. CREATIVITY & INNOVATION

• Dual-Axis Exploration: Decouples spatial selection from temporal variation, enabling planners to answer "What if launch slips 3 days?" with a single slider.

• Realregolith Perspective: Replaces abstract tabular data with an egocentric 360° horizon radar that lets planners see the crater skyline directly from the lander's perspective.

• Seamless Polar Cap Mesh: Solves the mathematical UV pole singularity on 3D globes by layering custom stereographic polar domes, eliminating texture pinching and rendering crisp polar craters.

5. FACTORS CONSIDERED & HONEST ACCOUNTING OF UNCERTAINTY

• Macro vs. Micro Hazards: MoonWindow clearly states that 267 m/pixel LOLA grids cannot resolve boulders below 10 meters or micro-crater hazards, which require lander hazard detection and avoidance (HDA) lidar.

• Geotechnical Stability: Regolith bearing capacity and trafficability require in-situ geotechnical telemetry. MoonWindow acts as an agile screening tool rather than certified autonomous landing software.

• Atmosphere-Free Horizon: Horizon calculations account for true geometric terrain elevation without atmospheric refraction.
